title: Pseudo-coherent complexes are quasi-coherent
statement: Let Y be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Every pseudo-coherent object E of D(\mathcal O_Y) [def-pc-derived-category, def-pur-pseudo-coherent-complex] belongs to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y), meaning that all its cohomology sheaves are quasi-coherent.

source.place: Tag 08EE proof, first sentence invoking Lemma lemma-pseudo-coherent

proof.text: By pseudo-coherence [def-pur-pseudo-coherent-complex], every point of Y has an open neighbourhood U on which E|_U is quasi-isomorphic to a bounded-above complex F^\bullet of finite free O_U-modules, so H^i(E)|_U \cong H^i(F^\bullet) for every i. Each term O_U^{\oplus n} is quasi-coherent [pqf-def-coherent] (on an affine open Spec A it is the module associated with A^{\oplus n}). H^i(F^\bullet) is the cokernel of the map F^{i-1} \to \ker(d^i), where \ker(d^i) is quasi-coherent as the kernel of a map of quasi-coherent modules [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-kernel], and this cokernel is quasi-coherent [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-cokernel-image]. Quasi-coherence is local on Y by its definition [pqf-def-coherent], so every H^i(E) is quasi-coherent, i.e. E lies in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(O_Y) [def-pc-derived-category].
